design.site_summary: A full-sun, low-moisture south-facing balcony inhabited by one dog who digs and chews.
design.layout_strategy: Upright shrubs and architectural plants form the mid-level layer against the warm back wall, while cascading herbs and trailing flowering annuals occupy the vertical railing boxes, and low mat-forming groundcovers carpet the floor-level containers out of direct dog-digging reach.
design.combination_logic: The scheme combines fine needle-like foliage of rosemary and thyme with the bold, cascading ribbons of the ponytail palm and the vibrant flower heads of lantana and yarrow. This creates a strong structural contrast in height and texture, releasing aromatic scents when brushed by the wind and providing continuous summer blooms that transition into warm autumn tones.

zones.placement: On the south-facing balcony railing, receiving 6+ hours of intense direct sun.

plants.why: Thrives in full sun, tolerates drought, and provides a safe, aromatic nibble for the household dog.
plants.role_in_combination: Forms a soft, scented trailing edge over the front of the planter boxes, contrasting with the upright plants behind it.

plants.why: Loves hot, dry conditions and spills over container edges with abundant golden flowers.
plants.role_in_combination: Adds bright yellow color splashes that weave through the thyme, creating a lively textural contrast.

maintenance: Water thoroughly when the top two inches of soil are dry.
Prune back thyme lightly after flowering to maintain dense growth.
Feed with a balanced organic liquid fertilizer once a month in summer.

zones.placement: Against the back wall of the balcony, bathed in intense afternoon sun and radiant heat.

plants.why: Extremely drought-tolerant architectural focal point that stores water in its swollen base.
plants.role_in_combination: Provides strong vertical presence and exotic curved foliage that contrasts against flat walls.

plants.why: Woody shrub that relishes baking sun and requires minimal water.
plants.role_in_combination: Offers evergreen height and a pungent woody scent that balances the soft floral elements.

plants.why: Heat-loving shrubby perennial producing vibrant multi-colored flower clusters all summer.
plants.role_in_combination: Delivers rich color transitions and a bushy mid-layer presence that bridges the palm and the herbs.

maintenance: Water deeply but infrequently, allowing soil to dry completely between waterings.
Prune lantana back by one-third in early spring to encourage dense branching.
Repot the ponytail palm every 2 to 3 years in spring into a slightly larger container with exceptional drainage.

zones.placement: Floor-level containers positioned along the inner perimeter of the balcony, sheltered from heavy dog paws.

plants.why: Tough, sun-loving perennial with fern-like foliage that handles dry soils effortlessly.
plants.role_in_combination: Provides flat-topped flower clusters and feathery leaf texture that contrasts with the needle-like rosemary.

maintenance: Water once a week during peak summer months.
Cut back spent yarrow flower stalks in late autumn to encourage fresh basal foliage.
Divide clumps every spring if they outgrow their containers.

care_instructions.task: Check soil moisture across all containers to account for the drying effects of the south-facing exposure.
care_instructions.frequency: Twice a week in summer, weekly in spring and autumn

care_instructions.task: Apply a low-nitrogen, slow-release organic fertilizer to promote blooming without excessive soft growth.
Inspect plants for spider mites and scale, which thrive in hot, dry balcony microclimates.

care_cautions: Lantana camara foliage can be toxic if ingested in large quantities by pets, so ensure the dog focuses its chewing strictly on the designated grazing thyme in the lower railing basket.
The southern exposure can cause rapid soil dessication and extreme heat stress; pots must have reliable drainage holes to prevent root damage while ensuring they do not dry out completely.
Tender perennials like Lantana may suffer frost damage during winter cold snaps and should be moved closer to the protected back wall or brought indoors.
design.pet_safety_note: The design keeps the dog safe by confining toxic shrubby elements to mid-level containers while providing an easily accessible, non-toxic patch of thyme on the railing for safe chewing and grazing.
